q-37950.name: Question 1
q-37950.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x{cos}^{2}⁡y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}[{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}[-\operatorname{cot}⁡x]_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}(-\operatorname{cot}⁡\frac{3\pi }{4}+\operatorname{cot}⁡\frac{\pi }{2})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}(-(-1)+0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡y}\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{sec}^{2}⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\operatorname{tan}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\frac{\pi }{4}-\operatorname{tan}⁡0 \\  & =1-0 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

∫0π/4[∫π/23π/41sin2⁡xcos2⁡ydx]dy=∫0π/41cos2⁡y[∫π/23π/41sin2⁡xdx]dy=∫0π/41cos2⁡y[−cot⁡x]π/23π/4dy=∫0π/41cos2⁡y(−cot⁡3π4+cot⁡π2)dy=∫0π/41cos2⁡y(−(−1)+0)dy=∫0π/41cos2⁡ydy

q-129549.name: Question 2
q-129549.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant. 

Making a substitution $x+y=u,$ $\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{y}^{1+y}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[-\frac{1}{u}]}_{y}^{1+y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(-\frac{1}{y+1}+\frac{1}{y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{y+1}]\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{y+1}]\,\text{d}y & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡y-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)]_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{y+1}){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

a
 −ln⁡(23)
b
 ln⁡(43)
c
1+ln⁡(12)
d
 ln⁡(12)
e
 ln⁡(12)+3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to x, treating y as a constant.

Making a substitution x+y=u, dx=du, we get.

∫12∫011(x+y)2dxdy=∫12[∫011(x+y)2dx]dy=∫12[∫y1+y1u2du]dy=∫12[−1u]y1+ydy=∫12(−1y+1+1y)dy=∫12[1y−1y+1]dy

Then, we integrate with respect to y:

∫12[1y−1y+1]dy=[ln⁡y−ln⁡(y+1)]12=ln⁡(yy+1)|12=ln⁡(23)−ln⁡(12)=ln⁡(23)+ln⁡(2)=ln⁡(23⋅2)=ln⁡(43)

q-37951.name: Question 3
q-37951.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}(1+{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{(1+{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡x]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{arctan}⁡0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\frac{\pi }{3}-0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{\pi }{3{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{\pi }{3{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & ={[-\frac{\pi }{3y}]}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3\cdot (-1)}-(-\frac{\pi }{3\cdot (-2)}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

q-72198.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le e,\,0\le y\le 2\}.$
q-72198.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{y}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]_{1}^{e}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(e)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

q-72197.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1\}.$
q-72197.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y[{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y(\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{y}{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{y}{2}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

q-73591.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,{e}^{2}\le x\le {e}^{4},\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{6}\}.$
q-73591.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{4}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}\cdot 2\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{2}{3}[{y}^{3}]_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}((\sqrt[3]{6})^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

q-129568.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{4},\,0\le y\le \pi \}.$
q-129568.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

Making a substitution $x+y=u,$ $\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[{\int }_{y}^{y+\pi /4}\operatorname{cos}⁡u\,\text{d}u]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡u]_{y}^{y+\pi /4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡y]\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }[\operatorname{sin}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{sin}⁡y]\text{d}y & ={[\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{cos}⁡(y+\frac{\pi }{4})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\  & =(-1+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})-(1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =\sqrt{2}-2\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Evaluate the double integral ∬Dcos⁡(x+y)dA, where D={(x,y):0≤x≤π4,0≤y≤π}.

a
 1
b
 2−2
c
 0
d
 22
e
 22−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:

∬Dcos⁡(x+y)dA=∫0π[∫0π/4cos⁡(x+y)dx]dy

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to x, treating y as a constant:

Making a substitution x+y=u, dx=du, we get.

∫0π[∫0π/4cos⁡(x+y)dx]dy=∫0π[∫yy+π/4cos⁡udu]dy=∫0π[sin⁡u]yy+π/4dy=∫0π[sin⁡(y+π4)−sin⁡y]dy

Finally, we integrate with respect to y:

∫0π[sin⁡(y+π4)−sin⁡y]dy=[cos⁡y−cos⁡(y+π4)]0π=(cos⁡(π)−cos⁡(5π4))−(cos⁡0−cos⁡(π4))=(−1+22)−(1−22)=2−2

q-73603.name: Question 12
q-73603.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{5}^{y}}{x}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{x}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{5}^{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{x}{[\frac{{5}^{y}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{x}(\frac{{5}^{1}-{5}^{0}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{1}{x}(\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{5}\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{1}^{5} \\  & =\frac{4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

q-71931.name: Question 13
q-71931.problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le \sqrt{2},\,0\le y\le 1\}.$

I. ${∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$

II. ${∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$

III. ${∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$
q-71931.worked_solution:
We notice that:

- the limits for the variable $x$ are from $1$ to $\sqrt{2}$, and

- the limits for the variable $y$ are from $0$ to $1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the region of integration is rectangular, we can simply swap the order of integration. This gives

$$
{∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x.
$$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only".
